text: We are starting our Saturday class, so thanks for being here. It's quite a good time for this Saturday. As you may remember, we now look at the MAC layers of Wi-Fi. And as we will see in Wi-Fi, we have two different schemes for accessing the channel. One is called DCF, Distributed Coordination Function. This is a distributed scheme, as the name says, and it is the one that is actually implemented in our Wi-Fi cards. Actually, nowadays we have an evolved version of it, but we will first look at the basic version of this scheme. The second one is called Point Coordination Function. This is a centralized access scheme. We will understand better what distributed and centralized access scheme means. The DCF is in the standard, it is specified by the standard, but it is not implemented in our phone. So we will focus on the first one that is actually implemented. We will just say a few words about the second one, and we will.
